name: LetterPress – Email Marketing, SMTP, Newsletter & Multi-Brand Subscriber Manager
author: themeqx

sections.description:
Stop renting your email marketing. Own it, and save up to 90%.

LetterPress helps you manage your newsletter and email campaigns directly from WordPress. Build campaigns, grow a consent-based subscriber list, organize contacts into groups and sources, and control how your emails are delivered, all from one admin area.

Whether you send product updates, announcements, or regular newsletters, LetterPress gives you the tools to manage the process without needing a separate email marketing dashboard.

Create campaigns that fit your message

Build emails with a title, message, button, supporting content, and footer. Preview your campaign in a browser, send a test email before launch, or schedule it for a future date. Personalize messages with the {{name}} merge tag, and let subscribers view the email in their browser when needed.

  • Create, edit, duplicate, schedule, pause, and resume campaigns.
  • Target all subscribers, a group, or a specific source.
  • Set a sender name and email address for each campaign when needed.
  • Preview campaign emails and send a test before sending to your audience.
  • See campaign progress and review per-campaign sending reports.
  • Replay a sent campaign’s preview any time.
  • Use sanitized, email-friendly rich text instead of arbitrary HTML or scripts.

Manage subscribers and grow your list

Collect signups with a consent-based form, confirm addresses with double opt-in, and keep your audience organized as your list grows.

  • Add a signup form to any page with the [letterpress_signup] shortcode.
  • Add a configurable subscription box with [letterpress_subscribe_box].
  • Enable double opt-in with signed confirmation links.
  • Import subscribers from CSV or export your subscriber list.
  • Import existing WordPress users as subscribers with a count preview.
  • Organize subscribers into groups and filter by source or status.
  • Search, paginate, block, unsubscribe, or delete subscribers in bulk.
  • Protect signup forms with a built-in math challenge and IP-based rate limiting.

Send with the provider you choose

Choose the delivery method that works for your site. LetterPress sends through the selected provider, while keeping other provider settings available if you switch later.

  • Amazon SES: Connect with AWS IAM credentials, choose a region, test the connection, and view the available sending quota.
  • SMTP: Configure your mail host, port, encryption, and credentials, then test the connection and authentication.
  • WordPress mail: Send through the standard wp_mail() mail path.
  • Site-wide email delivery: Optionally route WordPress emails through Amazon SES or SMTP.
  • Protected credentials: Provider credentials are encrypted before storage.

Keep sending organized and reliable

LetterPress uses a resumable queue to process campaigns in manageable batches. If a worker stops, queued work can continue later instead of requiring you to restart the campaign manually.

  • Configure the maximum number of recipients allowed within a rolling time window.
  • Set worker batch size independently from the sending rate.
  • Set a daily sending limit to help manage provider quotas.
  • Retry eligible failures automatically with backoff.
  • Protect against duplicate sends when a worker stops during delivery.
  • Schedule queue processing with WordPress cron or configure a server scheduler.
  • Follow the Cron Setup instructions for cPanel, Plesk, VPS/SSH, Cloudways, RunCloud, Windows Server, and managed hosting.

Actual sending speed depends on your provider’s limits, daily quota, server scheduler, network latency, and retries. A batch size controls how many queued emails a worker handles at once; it does not increase the configured sending rate.

Support multiple signup sources

Use sources to keep subscribers from different websites, forms, or brands (Source) organized. Each source can have its own display name, website, sender details, and double opt-in message.

  • Create as many sources as you need and view audience counts for each.
  • Set a default From name, From email, and Reply-To address per source.
  • Customize the confirmation email subject and body for each source.
  • Use stable source keys for forms and API integrations.
  • Safely reassign subscribers before deleting a source.

LetterPress also registers legacy sources for existing subscriber records. The default Website form source cannot be deleted, so at least one source remains available.

Help protect deliverability and subscriber preferences

Give subscribers a clear way to manage their email preferences and help prevent future sends to addresses that should not receive campaigns.

  • Include a personalized unsubscribe link in each campaign footer.
  • Add List-Unsubscribe headers for supported email clients.
  • Maintain a suppression list for manually blocked addresses, hard bounces, and complaints.
  • Automatically suppress addresses reported as bounced or complained about through Amazon SES/SNS events.
  • Optionally track opens with a signed tracking pixel.
  • Add your organization’s postal address to campaign footers.

Email and privacy requirements vary by location and use case. LetterPress provides tools to support responsible email practices, but using the plugin does not by itself guarantee legal compliance.

Connect your own systems with the REST API

Use API keys to connect forms, websites, or other applications to LetterPress.

  • Create labeled API keys and revoke them when needed.
  • Add subscribers through the REST API with Bearer authentication.
  • Retrieve a paginated list of subscribed addresses and filter by source.
  • Endpoints: POST /wp-json/letterpress/v1/add-subscriber and GET /wp-json/letterpress/v1/subscribers.
  • Validate source keys and reject requests for inactive sources.
  • Store API keys as hashes rather than plain-text secrets.

API keys are shown in full only when created, so save the key securely before leaving the page. Use HTTPS for API requests and never put a key in a URL.

Manage everything from one WordPress dashboard

Use the LetterPress admin area to review your audience and manage your email workflow.

  • Dashboard totals for subscribers, WordPress users, campaigns, and emails sent.
  • Campaign, subscriber, group, and source management.
  • Provider, sender identity, sending limit, deliverability, frontend, and event tracking settings.
  • API key management, subscription box settings, and cron setup instructions.
  • Responsive admin screens with a custom, app-style interface.
  • Capability checks on admin pages and actions.
  • Versioned, non-destructive database upgrades.

Delivery and tracking notes

Amazon SES event tracking uses an HTTPS endpoint for SNS notifications such as delivery, bounce, complaint, and rejection. SNS subscriptions are confirmed and event signatures are verified before processing. Duplicate events are ignored, and bounced or complained-about addresses can be added to the suppression list automatically.

For campaign delivery, make sure your chosen provider is configured correctly and that the sender address is authorized by that provider. For Amazon SES, you are responsible for completing the required AWS and DNS setup, including sender verification and appropriate email authentication records.

Reliable Email Delivery for Your WordPress Site

Not running email campaigns? LetterPress still has you covered.

LetterPress can handle your website’s everyday WordPress emails through your configured SMTP server. From password reset links and new user notifications to admin alerts and form notifications, your essential emails can be delivered reliably without needing a separate SMTP plugin.

Connect your preferred SMTP provider, configure your sender details, and let LetterPress handle your site’s outgoing email. You can use it purely as an SMTP mailer, even if you never send a newsletter or marketing campaign.

What You Can Do

  • Replace Your SMTP Plugin: Configure SMTP directly in LetterPress instead of installing a separate plugin just for email delivery.
  • Deliver WordPress Emails: Send password reset emails, user registration notifications, admin alerts, and other default WordPress emails through your configured mail server.
  • Connect Your Preferred Provider: Use a supported SMTP server or email delivery service to send your site’s outgoing emails.
  • Keep Everything in One Place: Manage SMTP settings alongside your newsletters, email campaigns, and subscriber lists from a single plugin.

One plugin for everyday WordPress emails and email marketing. Use the SMTP features independently, then explore newsletters and campaigns whenever you’re ready.

More Powerful Tools Are on the Way

We’re working on new features to make LetterPress even more useful. Visual email template building and marketing automation are currently under development and will be available in future updates.

Coming Soon

  • Email Template Builder: Create beautiful, professional emails with an easier visual editing experience, without needing to write code.
  • Marketing Automation: Set up automated email sequences, welcome emails, and follow-ups to engage your subscribers at the right time.

We’re building these features to help you manage more of your email marketing from one place. Stay tuned for upcoming updates.

Report a Bug

Found a bug or something not working as expected? Please contact our team with a description of the issue and steps to reproduce it. Your feedback helps us improve LetterPress for everyone.
sections.installation:
1. Install LetterPress through the WordPress Plugins screen or upload the plugin to /wp-content/plugins/letterpress.
  2. Activate LetterPress. The plugin runs its versioned database upgrade automatically.
  3. Go to LetterPress > Settings and select your delivery provider.
  4. Configure your sender identity and sending limits.
  5. Test your provider connection and send a test email before launching a campaign.
  6. Add [letterpress_signup] to a page to display the signup form. Configure double opt-in in settings if you want subscribers to confirm their addresses.
  7. Open LetterPress > Cron Setup and follow the instructions for your hosting environment. For reliable queue processing, configure a server scheduler to request the displayed WordPress cron URL every minute.

Amazon SES setup

  1. Create AWS IAM credentials with the required SES sending permissions and ses:GetAccount for quota reporting.
  2. Verify the sender email address or domain in the same AWS region you select in LetterPress.
  3. Configure Easy DKIM and the appropriate SPF and DMARC records in DNS. You may also configure a custom MAIL FROM domain.
  4. To process delivery feedback, configure an SES configuration set with an SNS event destination for delivery, bounce, complaint, and rejection events.
  5. Set the matching SNS topic ARN in LetterPress and subscribe the plugin’s displayed HTTPS event endpoint to the topic.

DNS verification and AWS account configuration are handled outside LetterPress. Make sure your hosting environment allows the outbound HTTPS requests required for SNS confirmation and verification.

SMTP setup

Enter the SMTP host, port, encryption method, and login credentials in the provider settings. Use the built-in connection and authentication test before sending a campaign.
sections.faq:
Which email delivery methods does LetterPress support?

LetterPress supports Amazon SES through its API, generic SMTP, and standard WordPress mail. Only the selected provider sends emails. Settings for other providers are retained so you can switch later.

Can I schedule a campaign?

Yes. You can schedule a campaign for a future date and time. LetterPress starts it when the scheduled time arrives, provided WordPress cron or your server scheduler is running.

Can I test an email before sending it to subscribers?

Yes. Configure the test recipient in LetterPress settings and send a test campaign before starting the full send.

Can I personalize emails?

Yes. Use {{name}} in the subject or message body. If a subscriber does not have a name, LetterPress uses “there” as the fallback.

How does LetterPress handle sending limits?

You can configure a maximum number of recipients per rolling time window and a separate worker batch size. You can also set a daily limit. Provider quotas, scheduling, network conditions, and retries can affect the actual sending speed.

What happens if sending stops partway through a campaign?

LetterPress keeps the queue so eligible work can resume when the worker runs again. If a worker stops while an email is in flight and delivery is uncertain, that item is marked as failed rather than automatically resent, helping avoid duplicate emails.

Can subscribers unsubscribe?

Yes. Campaigns include a personalized unsubscribe link and List-Unsubscribe headers. Unsubscribed, blocked, and suppressed addresses are excluded from future campaigns.

Can I manage multiple brands or signup forms?

Yes. Create sources for different websites, forms, or brands. Each source can have its own sender identity and double opt-in message, and you can target a campaign to a particular source.

Can I import existing contacts?

You can import subscribers from a CSV file or import existing WordPress users as subscribers. You can also export subscriber data to CSV.

Can I connect LetterPress to another application?

Yes. The REST API lets authenticated applications add subscribers and retrieve a paginated list of subscribed addresses. Create API keys under LetterPress > API Keys. Keep keys private and send requests over HTTPS.

Does LetterPress guarantee legal compliance or email delivery?

No plugin can guarantee legal compliance or inbox placement on its own. You are responsible for collecting appropriate consent, following the laws that apply to your audience, configuring your sending provider and DNS records, and maintaining your subscriber list.

Found a bug or need help?

If you find a bug, have a question, or need help with LetterPress, please contact our team. You can also visit the Themeqx website to learn more about our products.
sections.changelog:
2.4.0

  • Added subscriber source management with safe deletion and subscriber reassignment.
  • Added per-source sender identity settings for From name, From email, and Reply-To.
  • Added source filtering on the Subscribers page and an index on the subscriber source column.
  • Added REST API endpoints to add subscribers and list subscribed addresses using Bearer API key authentication.

2.2.0

  • Updated sending limits to use a shared, concurrency-safe rolling recipient rate limiter and an independently configured worker batch size.
  • Added interval-in-seconds settings with a backward-compatible migration from interval minutes.

2.1.2

  • Improved primary action button text contrast and refined admin typography.

2.1.1

  • Refreshed the admin dashboard, settings, forms, and tables with a responsive app-style interface.

2.1.0

  • Added structured campaign templates, provider settings, subscriber signup and import/export, campaign scheduling, SES quota-aware limits, and SNS event tracking.
  • Added versioned, non-destructive database migrations and improved credential protection.

1.1.2

  • Fixed a class loading issue on Windows.

1.1.1

  • Added lp_strip_tags() to clean campaign HTML body content.

1.1.0

  • Improved HTML sanitization and campaign message cleaning.
  • Fixed several issues with stored and displayed HTML content.

1.0.0

  • Initial release.
